classification.difficultyReason: Use the intersections to bound the segment, express its vertical length as upper ordinate minus lower ordinate, and maximise that new quadratic by symmetry.

content.prompt: The graphs of $y=x-x^2$ and $y=x^2-5x$ are drawn on the same number plane.

spec.sourceRegion: Left column, question 18, between the shared stem and part (a).
spec.description: Two contrasting parabolas on black axes. The blue parabola opens downwards; the red parabola opens upwards. Black points P and Q share an abscissa, with P above Q, and a dashed vertical segment joins them. Both curves have arrowheads at both displayed ends. There are no numerical ticks, grid lines, origin label or printed curve-equation labels.
spec.mathematics: Plot y=x-x^2 and y=x^2-5x directly from their equations. P lies on the first curve and Q on the second, between their intersections. Their common abscissa is schematic and unlabelled; its numerical value is not a source given. The shown upper-minus-lower relationship supports restricting the separation calculation to the interval between the intersections.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source-supplied curves, axes, points P and Q and dashed segment are visible. Intersection coordinates and the maximum separation are not supplied.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the points of intersection of the two graphs.

answer.worked:
Equate the expressions for $y$.

$$\begin{align*}x-x^2&=x^2-5x\\2x^2-6x&=0\\2x(x-3)&=0\\x&=0\text{ or }3.\end{align*}$$

Substitute into $y=x-x^2$. When $x=0$, $y=0$. When $x=3$, $y=3-3^2=-6$.

The intersection points are $(0,0)$ and $(3,-6)$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the largest possible length of $PQ$.

inlines.text: ; its maximum lies halfway between its zeros.

answer.worked:
Between the intersections, $0\le x\le3$ and $P$ lies above $Q$.

$$\begin{align*}PQ&=(x-x^2)-(x^2-5x)\\PQ&=6x-2x^2\\PQ&=2x(3-x).\end{align*}$$

This quadratic is concave down and has zeros $0$ and $3$. Its maximum occurs halfway between them, at $x=\frac32$.

$$\begin{align*}PQ_{\max}&=2\left(\frac32\right)\left(3-\frac32\right)\\PQ_{\max}&=\frac92\text{ units}.\end{align*}$$
